sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Genesee County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Deeds for Genesee County land are recorded at the County Clerk and Register of Deeds in the Genesee County Administration Building, 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed on county holidays.

One elected office runs three divisions: vital records, elections and the register of deeds. The register keeps deeds, mortgages, liens and other papers that affect real estate in the county. The county's own page says that recording a document does not make it legal, only public. The register's job is to index the paper into a searchable database and keep the record intact, so a deed with a defect stays defective after it is recorded.

sections.h2: What does the Genesee County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
Michigan's default fee is $30 per recorded document, no matter how many pages it has. A charter county may set its own schedule by ordinance, so ask the office for its current fee sheet before you mail a check.

Service under MCL 600.2567Fee
Record a document, any page count$30.00
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged in one document$3.00 added
Copies of records$1.00 per page
Certify a recorded document$5.00
Search by grantor or grantee50 cents per year searched, $5.00 minimum
File any other paper$1.00

Source: Michigan Compiled Laws 600.2567. The $30 includes the state remonumentation fee, and $5 of every recording goes into the county automation fund.

The fee is due when the document is left for recording. If the register accepts electronic documents and the fee is paid electronically, the statute allows payment within one business day of receipt. Ask the office whether it takes e-recording, and which submitters it works with, before you plan around it.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes due when a Genesee County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
A deed for money triggers two taxes, one to the state and one to the county, and both are the seller's to pay. The state charges $3.75 for each $500 of value, and the county charges 55 cents for each $500, since its population is under two million.

The deed must state the total value of the real estate on its face, or an affidavit of value must be attached. If a sale includes both land and personal property, tax applies only to the land when the two values are stated separately. The tax goes to the Genesee County Treasurer within 15 days after the seller delivers the deed. On a $120,000 sale the figures are 240 units of $500, which gives $900 to the state and $132 to the county.

  • No tax: instruments for less than $100, mortgages and other security documents, leases and court orders that set no price.
  • Family transfers: a deed from a person to a child, stepchild, grandchild or adopted child is exempt from the state tax.
  • Foreclosure: a document given in foreclosure, or in lieu of it, is exempt, though a later sale by the foreclosing party is not.
  • Land contracts: exempt while legal title stays with the seller until the full price is paid.
  • Title cleanup: a corrective quitclaim that only confirms title the buyer already holds.

If you paid tax on a transfer that qualified for an exemption, the state's transfer tax act lets the seller, or a buyer who paid on the seller's behalf, ask the Department of Treasury for a refund.

sections.h2: Which papers usually get recorded in a Genesee County home sale?
sections.html:
A typical sale produces a deed and, if there was a mortgage, a discharge of that mortgage. Each paper is recorded separately and carries its own fee, with the $3 add-on if a single discharge covers more than one instrument.

  • Deed: warranty, quitclaim or personal representative deed, with value stated.
  • Discharge or assignment of mortgage: $30 plus $3 for each extra instrument covered.
  • Tax foreclosure papers: certificates of forfeiture and redemption, notices of judgment of foreclosure, and deeds out of a foreclosure sale. The statute lets those fees be paid within 30 days of the sale or transfer, or on a date agreed with the foreclosing unit.
  • Property transfer affidavit: not a register of deeds filing. It goes to the city or township assessor, which in Flint is the city's Assessments Division.

Ask the register's office which of these it can record electronically and which it wants on paper, since the county's page does not list accepted formats.

sections.h2: What does a tax foreclosure judgment do to the recorded title in Genesee County?
sections.html:
It wipes out most recorded claims against the parcel. When a foreclosure judgment takes effect on March 31, title vests in the foreclosing governmental unit, which in Genesee is the county treasurer, and liens and interests on the parcel are extinguished. The state's timeline lists the survivors: future special assessment installments, environmental liens filed by governmental agencies, severed or leased oil and gas interests, visible or recorded easements and private deed restrictions.

Those papers end up in the register's index. A notice of judgment of foreclosure and later the deed from the auction are recorded here, and the statute lets the recording fee for those two documents be paid within 30 days of the sale or transfer. For an owner, the practical point is the date. Until the March 31 effective date a parcel can still be redeemed by paying the taxes, interest and fees, and after it the owner has no right to the house. Genesee County's treasurer holds the online auctions, and the recorded deed from that sale is what a new owner relies on.

sections.h2: Which Genesee County office holds which record?
sections.html:
Four offices hold the records you are most likely to need, and the register is the only one that holds the recorded documents themselves.

  • Register of Deeds: deeds, mortgages, discharges, liens and foreclosure notices, at 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A.
  • Equalization, Suite 8B: parcel descriptions and land records for every municipality except Flint. Its page sends owners to the local assessor for assessment data.
  • Flint Assessments Division: parcel records for Flint, plus property transfer affidavits, land splits and combinations.
  • County Treasurer, Suite 2A: delinquent tax payoffs and foreclosure information.

Before a sale, order the payoff from the treasurer if taxes are delinquent, and check with the assessor that the parcel description matches the deed.

sections.h2: Why does the Genesee County deed record matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Because the record is the public chain of title, and a buyer or a title company reads it before closing. An unrecorded discharge or a deed with a misspelled name is the kind of gap that has to be fixed before the sale can finish.

The county's housing numbers show how much property moves through the office. The Census Bureau counts 185,007 housing units and 167,334 households, with owners in 70.7% of homes and a median owner-occupied value of $182,400. Flint's median value is $53,500. Genesee borders Tuscola, Lapeer, Oakland, Livingston, Shiawassee and Saginaw counties, and I-75, I-69 and I-475 cross its middle.

A seller who inherits a house, owes back tax or cannot afford repairs can sell it as-is to a cash buyer. The deed and any mortgage discharge are recorded at this office, and unpaid taxes are paid from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Genesee County?
faqs.a: The state default under MCL 600.2567 is $30 for a document of any length. Charter counties can set their own fees, so confirm the current Genesee County amount with the register's office before you send payment.

faqs.q: Where is the Genesee County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is in the Genesee County Administration Building at 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. The county's page lists Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., excluding holidays.

faqs.q: Does recording a deed make it legally valid?
faqs.a: No. The county's own page says that recording makes a document public, and does not make it legal. A deed still needs proper signing, a correct description and a grantor who owns the property.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Genesee County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays both the state tax of $3.75 per $500 and the county tax of 55 cents per $500. The payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed.

faqs.q: Is a deed to my child exempt from transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes, a conveyance from an individual to a child, stepchild, adopted child, grandchild or step-grandchild is on the state's exemption list. The deed is still recorded and the recording fee still applies.
